content:
In the wave of AI agents massively requesting "full disk access" on Mac, Apple has stated it will make changes to macOS to protect user privacy.

Although Apple has not yet revealed specific details, it emphasised that users should understand the implications of granting such "special" access to applications.

Apple explained in a blog post on its Developer website that macOS full disk access was originally intended to "allow backup applications to function properly on Mac." However, Apple pointed out that "some developers" are using the macOS full disk access setting in ways that "could put users at risk."

Apple responded by saying it would "introduce additional control mechanisms to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant applications this special level of access must do so through a very explicit user action."

The company has not revealed any further details about these control measures or related changes. Nonetheless, Apple stated that with the rise of "increasingly powerful and autonomous" AI agents, privacy and security need greater attention:

Apple's announcement comes at a time when tools such as Meta Muse and OpenAI's Dots are growing in popularity. These round-the-clock AI agents request access to large amounts of personal data, and there have already been some alarming cases, particularly on the Meta Muse side.
